invariants.name: agent_unique
invariants.statement: exactly one cell shows colour 6 at all times

invariants.name: nothing_rests_on_a_free_cell
invariants.statement: the cell below the agent and below every movable is never free — every state a reader can observe is a settle fixpoint, so there is nowhere left to fall

invariants.name: block_count
invariants.statement: exactly 1 cell(s) show colour 2 at all times

invariants.name: blocks_disjoint
invariants.statement: no two blocks ever occupy the same cell

invariants.name: single_armed_tile
invariants.statement: at most one fragile tile is armed at any instant

invariants.name: armed_tile_under_agent
invariants.statement: an armed fragile tile's cell is the agent's cell

invariants.name: tile_state_is_monotone
invariants.note: prose only — not checkable on a single state
invariants.statement: a fragile tile's state only ever rises, 0 -> 1 -> 2, so a collapsed tile is never crossed again

claims.claimed: conditional — reversible on open floor, not across a one-way edge
conditional — only where the agent can reach the far side of the block

rules.name: walk
rules.reversible: conditional — reversible on open floor, not across a one-way edge
rules.then: the agent moves one cell in direction D
rules.when: act=D and the target cell is inside the grid, is not a wall, and no mechanism claims it

rules.name: blocked_by_wall
rules.when: act=D and the target cell is outside the grid or is a wall

rules.name: fall
rules.then: that thing descends one cell, and this repeats to a fixpoint — a post-step settlement, appended to whatever rule ended the step, never tagged as a rule of its own
rules.when: the cell directly below the agent, or below a movable entity, is free
rules.why: descending a ledge cannot be undone from below, so a fall is a one-way edge in the reachable graph and any rule witnessed only above a ledge gets exactly one witness

rules.name: up_is_inert
rules.then: the agent enters the cell above if that cell is free, then falls back into the cell it left during the same step's settlement, so the state after the step equals the state before it

rules.name: push
rules.reversible: conditional — only where the agent can reach the far side of the block
rules.then: the block moves one cell in direction D and the agent takes the block's old cell
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a block and the cell beyond it in direction D is free

rules.name: blocked_by_block
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a block and the cell beyond it is not free

rules.name: cross_fragile
rules.then: the agent moves onto the tile and the tile arms.  The tile does not collapse on this step: the collapse happens later, in settlement, on the first step at which the agent is no longer standing there — so in the trace the tile changes to the collapsed colour one frame after the crossing, not in the frame of the crossing itself
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds an intact fragile tile

rules.name: blocked_by_collapsed
rules.when: act=D and the target cell holds a collapsed fragile tile

blocking_entities.verdict: removing it makes the world solvable in 6 steps

certificate.statement: the reachable set has 18 states and the agent occupies the goal cell (5, 7) in none of them

spec.notes: Gravity, a shovable block and two one-shot floors. Every descent is one-way and every crossing is one-shot, so the reachable graph is close to a DAG — the extreme opposite of `t1-cycler-gate`.
